visualMetaphor: a moneylender's wooden bench snapped in two, its halves turning into a banknote torn down the middle
title: Hanged for hiding his money
angle: In 1761 London hanged John Perrott, a Ludgate Hill bankrupt £13,513 short (about £3m today), under the 1706 act that made hiding assets from creditors a hanging crime. The money trail runs to banknotes cut in half in his prison trunk. The same act's afterthought, the discharge, outlived the rope: English bankrupts are still usually freed from their debts after 12 months.
